newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps mostly weak after gas oil falls har.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps mostly weak after gas oil falls har.

text.p: European oil swaps came under renewed downward pressure on Friday afternoon when a late drop in gas oil and gasoline undermined the wider market.
Gas oil futures ended $5.50 a tonne lower and differentials against the IPE for physical swaps were also under pressure.
In Northwest Europe EN590 swaps for May slipped $1 a tonne to $12.50 a tonne above the screen while 0.2 percent sulphur eased 50 cents to $4.50 over.
The Mediterranean swaps were little changed either side of $8, after falling $2 on Thursday.

Jet premiums also fell with sellers asking $24 a tonne over the screen for June and just under $27 over for the third quarter. "The brokers haven't got any bids so those numbers are probably a bit on the high side," said a trader.
Gasoline also fell hard. May swaps lost $4 a tonne as losses on Brent crude tugged the market lower. May was assessed around $194.25 by the close with June $2.50 lower.
"The cracks were unchanged, so most of the losses were cent for cent with crude," said a broker who saw crack spreads at $5.20 a barrel for May and $4.90.
Heavy fuel oil was little changed after reversing early $1 a tonne gains. May barges ended around $83.25 having talked over $84 at lunchtime.
Low sulphur stayed $3.50 a tonne higher in May while June was pegged around $84.50 on barges and $89 for low sulphur.
Despite the weakness some brokers struggled to find sellers on low sulphur, which has recently enjoyed some support from demand into Israel.
"We had a buyer at $88.50 for June and still couldn't find an offer," said a broker late in the afternoon.
Despite the losses elsewhere Brent CFDs were confused in late trading after gains on wet Brent which traded at just 20 cents under June.
On Thursday it had traded at both 25 and 37 cents under June.

Brent CFDs made gains of about 8 cents for next weeks dates which climbed to 25 cents under June. The following three weeks were little changed at 32 cents, 26 cents and 23 cents respectively. -- Sam Arnold-Forster, London Newsroom 171 542 4984
